text:
lisa: Heads up — EU-west GPU pool is spiking with long-lived streaming sessions and we're seeing a cascade where short non-stream batches are getting queued >30s and timing out. Noticing a lot of 502s from the routing layer.

mike: saw that. graphs show streaming session count doubled after the demo traffic at 14:20. streaming p99 token latency jumped, non-stream queue length hit the cap.

tara: is this the new chat model rollout? any model size differences causing slower per-token throughput?

lisa: it's a mix — some hosts are on the new 70B quantized variant (slower decode), plus a region-level network hiccup made the router backlog visible.

infra-bot: Deployment notice: drain of node pool eu-west-2b started at 14:35 for kernel patch. 8 nodes marked for cordon.

mike: ah that explains reduced headroom. cordon + long-lived streams = starvation for short jobs.

tara: can we tombstone streaming sessions on cordoned nodes or migrate them? eviction would cause UX regressions though.

lisa: migration is expensive (KV cache warmup). proposal: temporary priority-buckets — guaranteed min slots for non-streaming critical pipelines, and a streaming soft-cap that returns 429 when pool below threshold.

ben: +1 for guaranteed slots. Also suggest a short-term admission policy: if pool_util > 85% then throttle non-critical streaming at the router with header X-Infer-Priority.

mike: we already tag requests with priority but router doesn't enforce per-pool capacity. We'd need a quick ACL in the router to map priority->slot share. possible but needs a small hotfix.

tara: what about cost tradeoffs? raising dedicated capacity in eu-west for a day is costly but quick fix. Alternatively, divert low-priority streaming to another region (latency hit).

lisa: cost vs latency: temporary cross-region routing sounds acceptable for background sessions (we can set a 200ms tail SLA flag). Critical non-stream customers should stay local.

sre_oncall: meanwhile I'll pin autoscaler to ignore cordon for 20m window to avoid synchronized evictions, and enable graceful eviction for streaming workers so they stop accepting new streams but finish in-flight.

ben: example router rule (sketch):
```
if pool_util(eu-west) > 0.85:
  if req.header.x-infer-priority == "critical": allow
  elif req.header.x-infer-priority == "background": route->eu-central
  else: return 429 with Retry-After
```

mike: could also implement a small token-bucket per-priority on the frontend to smooth bursts. less invasive than altering allocator.

lisa: agreed. action items: 1) mike -> prototype per-priority token-bucket at router (15m) 2) sre_oncall -> set autoscaler guardrails and enable graceful drain (5m) 3) tara -> update ops playbook with cross-region fallback and cost estimate.

tara: I'll also add a note to the console team to expose pool_util and per-priority queue lengths on the dashboard so customers can see throttling.

mike: quick question — do we expose Retry-After semantics for streaming clients? some clients won't handle 429 well.

lisa: we can return structured JSON with fields {code, retry_after, fallback_region} and a header. add to playbook.

infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-eu-west-streaming-saturation (severity: medium)

ben: thanks. keeping an eye. will re-evaluate after token-bucket prototype. :thumbsup:

lisa: will post updates here when rules are live. thanks everyone.
